text:
A fourth-round pick from 2021 is on an 11-game point streak for the champions. Jackson Blake has 21 points in 21 games, and the reason is not a mystery: he plays 17:51 a night, up from 16:30, and is on the ice for 83% of Carolina's power-play time, up from 40%. The Hockey Writers have taken to calling him and Logan Stankoven a dangerous duo.

The luck cuts both ways. His own finishing is behind, 6 goals on 8.7 expected, so more goals should come. But Carolina has scored 5.8 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has inflated the assists. What is left is a real jump: his own chance rate is up to 1.40 expected goals per 60 minutes from 1.22.

The surroundings help. Carolina owns 66.3% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays, and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that his teammates ranked in the 96th percentile.

Our projection has him finishing between 56 and 79 points, 67 in the middle, after 39 goals and 48 assists in his first 162 games. What to watch: whether the power-play role sticks as the lineup fills back in.
